source.author: verg
source.text: Ipsa, Iovis rapidum iaculata e nubibus ignem, disiecitque rates evertitque aequora ventis, illum expirantem transfixo pectore flammas turbine corripuit scopuloque infixit acuto.
source.text_original: Ipsa, Iovis rapidum iaculata e nubibus ignem, / disiecitque rates evertitque aequora ventis, / illum expirantem transfixo pectore flammas / turbine corripuit scopuloque infixit acuto.
source.text_english: She herself, hurling Jove’s swift fire from the clouds, scattered the ships and overturned the seas with winds; that man, as he breathed out flames from his pierced breast, she snatched up in a whirlwind and fixed him on a sharp rock.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tum valida Clymenus percusso pectore tonsa frater et Iphiclus puppem trahit, et face saeva in tua mox Danaos acturus saxa, Caphereu, Nauplius, et tortum non a love fulmen Oileus qui gemet, Euboicas nato stridente per undas, quique Erymanthei sudantem pondere monstri Amphitryoniaden Tegeaeo limine Cepheus iuvit, et Amphidamas at frater plenior actis maluit Ancaeo vellus contingere Phrixi tectus et Eurytion servato colla capillo, quem pater Aonias reducem tondebit ad aras.
reuse.text_original: tum valida Clymenus percusso pectore tonsa / frater et Iphiclus puppem trahit, et face saeva / in tua mox Danaos acturus saxa, Caphereu, / Nauplius, et tortum non a love fulmen Oileus / qui gemet, Euboicas nato stridente per undas, / quique Erymanthei sudantem pondere monstri / Amphitryoniaden Tegeaeo limine Cepheus / iuvit, et Amphidamas (at frater plenior actis / maluit Ancaeo vellus contingere Phrixi) / tectus et Eurytion servato colla capillo, / quem pater Aonias reducem tondebit ad aras.
reuse.text_english: Then Clymenus, striking his breast, and Iphiclus with shorn hair, strong, haul the ship, and soon Nauplius, about to drive the Danaans with a cruel torch onto your rocks, Caphereus, and Oileus, who will groan at the twisted thunderbolt not from Jupiter, as it whistles over the Euboean waves for his son; and Cepheus, who helped Amphitryoniades, sweating under the weight of the Erymanthian monster, at the Tegean threshold; and Amphidamas, and his brother, fuller with deeds, preferred to touch the fleece of Phrixus with Ancaeus; and Eurytion, his hair preserved, whose neck his father, on his return, will cut at the Aonian altars.
